title: Solutions and Separating Mixtures
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: Solutions and Separating Mixtures Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe solutes, solvents, solubility and concentration; identify factors that affect the rate of dissolving; explain methods for separating mixtures and how they are used in industry and to protect the environment. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Pure Substances and Mixtures)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 science worksheets on solutes and solvents, solubility, concentration, saturated solutions, filtration, evaporation, chromatography and distillation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The solute dissolves in the solvent.
key_sub: Heat, stirring and small pieces speed up dissolving; filters, magnets and evaporation separate mixtures.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a solution, the solute dissolves in the solvent.

  • Solubility is how much solute can dissolve; a saturated solution can hold no more.
  • Dissolving is faster with higher temperature, stirring and smaller pieces.
  • Separation methods: sieving, filtering, magnets, evaporation, distillation and chromatography.
Example

Which method gets salt back from salt water?

the water can leave as vapour

Answer: evaporation

Example

A solution has 15 g of sugar in 50 mL. What is the concentration?

15 ÷ 50 = 0.3

Answer: 0.3 g/mL

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a dissolved solute has disappeared.
  • Thinking filtering can remove dissolved salt.
  • Mixing up solute and solvent.

faq.q: What is the difference between a solute and a solvent?
faq.a: The solute is what dissolves (like sugar). The solvent is what it dissolves in (like water).

faq.q: Why can you not filter salt out of salt water?
faq.a: The salt particles are dissolved and small enough to pass through the filter.

faq.q: Where is separation used in real life?
faq.a: Water treatment, recycling plants, oil refineries, mining and cleaning up spills.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about the condenser is correct?
c: It is what is left behind on the filter paper in filtration.
It cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.
It make the liquid boil smoothly.
It is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.
items.e: The condenser cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.

items.q: What is the principle behind filtration?
c: Only magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted to a magnet.
Insoluble solid particles are too big to pass through the tiny holes in the filter paper.
The liquid with the lower boiling point boils first, and its vapour is cooled and condensed.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
items.e: This is how filtration works.

items.q: Which separation technique works on this principle? The liquid with the lower boiling point boils first, and its vapour is cooled and condensed.

sets.title: Separation in industry and the environment

items.q: A student heats copper(II) sulfate solution until it is dry. Why might she stop before it is completely dry?
c: To get crystals instead of a powder that may decompose with too much heat.
To make it a liquid again.
items.e: Heat gently and let crystals form as it cools.

items.q: A recycling plant uses a large magnet on a moving belt. What does it remove?
items.e: Steel contains iron, which is magnetic.

items.q: How can you separate a mixture of cork pieces and gravel?
c: let it settle and pour off the top layer
add water and skim off what floats
items.e: Cork floats and gravel sinks.

items.q: Why must the solvent level be below the start line in paper chromatography?
c: So that the dyes do not dissolve straight into the solvent in the beaker.
So that the paper does not get wet.
So that the dyes move faster.
items.e: The solvent must carry the dyes up the paper.

items.q: Emma mixes 8 g of sand with 200 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: Ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. A mixture of the two is heated. Which liquid is collected first?
items.e: The liquid with the lower boiling point boils off first.

items.q: Which method separates sugar dissolved in water?
c: let it settle and pour off the top layer
